text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand, so developers can read and work with it more easily. When you refactor, the program should behave exactly the same as before — users should not notice any difference. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly and becomes messy over time. By regularly cleaning up and reorganizing the code, teams can avoid bigger problems later and keep their projects healthy and easier to maintain.
